analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - October 28, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: Rating changes: GTT (GTT.PA) upgraded to Buy from Neutral as an attractive entry point into a highly visible LNG growth story. Poste Italiane (PST.MI) reinstated at Neutral from Not Rated, with solid growth prospects but fair valuation. No rating changes in the Americas or Asia.

Target price cuts of 10% or more: Enphase (ENPH) to $40 from $47, Robinhood (HOOD) to $128 from $145, Whirlpool (WHR) to $35 from $41, Xylem (XYL) to $138 from $160. All keep their ratings (ENPH, HOOD, XYL Buy, WHR Neutral).

Target price raises of 10% or more: Kiniksa (KNSA) to $101 from $90 (Buy), TransUnion (TRU) to $78 from $68 (Neutral), Evolution Gaming (EVOG.ST) to Skr700 from Skr610 (Sell), Data#3 (DTL.AX) to A$13.75 from A$12.30 (Neutral).
Xylem is cut on growth concerns as slower revenue conversion drives a lower FY2026 outlook, but orders and margins remain robust, and the rating stays Buy.
Enphase's estimate reset is described as the latest sign of a bottoming residential solar cycle, with company-specific growth drivers key to recovery. Rating stays Buy.

Robinhood posted a modest core beat and constructive platform growth, with a slightly weaker transaction revenue outlook. SoFi and PayPal shares outperform on stronger growth outlook and modestly better EPS outlook respectively. Visa's F4Q26 was relatively in line with an F2027 outlook sustaining strong performance.

Consumer staples: Coca-Cola delivered a volume-led Q3 beat and raise, though structural headwinds are expected to temper EPS growth next year. Philip Morris is reiterated Buy and named a top stock idea on strong top and bottom line momentum. NielsenIQ data through 10/17 shows total alcoholic beverage sales still pressured with declines moderating slightly, nicotine sales declines moderating, and food sales decelerating on softer volumes.

Travel and leisure: Royal Caribbean (Maintain Buy) sees a favorable setup into next year with the 1H/2H cadence reset for net yield growth in 2027. Hilton (Maintain Buy) expects flow through to improve in 2027 as headwinds abate. Travel + Leisure is Maintain Buy with a $78 target.

Industrials and transport: Boeing's battle to get to normalized continues (Buy). UPS beat on EPS with domestic margin on track. Landstar missed on EPS on higher insurance costs. Johnson Controls sees orders re-accelerating with a conservative FY27 guide. Whirlpool shows declining demand visibility but is focusing on margins and cash flow.

Technology: S&P Global posted a 3Q beat-and-raise, with the strategic review of CapIQ a potential source of value creation. Celestica's analyst day gave a better-than-expected 2027 EPS, revenue and margin outlook. Seagate had a solid quarter relative to elevated expectations, but shifting industry dynamics are likely to cap HDD multiples. F5 guided F2027 in line. NXP's 2027 outlook is intact with increased capital returns.
Memory chips: a TrendForce expert session reaffirmed a strong 2027 DRAM/HBM outlook, and GS reiterates Buy on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

Healthcare: Vertex and Amgen 3Q earnings previews are published, with the Vertex focus on IgAN approval and launch ahead of an eventful 4Q and beyond. Novartis had a strong 3Q26 profit beat driven by cost control, but valuation stays full and the Sell rating is kept.

Europe: Danone Q3 volume/mix was below expectations with a US leadership change. Traton's 3Q26 miss is likely to cut 2027 adjusted EPS consensus by a low single digit percentage. KONE missed in 3Q and narrowed guidance. Saint-Gobain reiterated margin guidance but volume deceleration is more visible. Bank first looks are published for UBS, Santander, BNP Paribas and Deutsche Bank.

Asia: Japan Banks note quantifies risk factors after a correction and looks for value. Shin-Etsu Chemical's Q2 beat and unchanged full-year guidance look conservative as customers prioritize supply security (Buy). Boss Energy and PLS Group are rated Sell on relative valuation. Woolworths is Neutral but preferred over Coles.

Macro and strategy notes flagged: Global Markets Daily on macro assets in Fed hiking cycles, a mortgage note saying the executive order on housing is unlikely to have a large immediate impact, and a China rates-to-equities replay.
Galaxy Digital (GLXY) shows healthy operating trends in 3Q26 against a more challenging data center financing backdrop.
